scope: Primary-source literature verification for research stage only; no new experiments or manuscript edits

sources.title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
sources.publication_status_verified: Published conference paper, official USENIX entry and proceedings PDF
full_text_read_locators: Section 5.1: setup, targets, metrics, human validation
Section 5: ablations on attack count and retrieval depth
sources.establishes: Evaluates retrieval and generation separately; validates substring-based ASR against author human judgments.
sources.does_not_establish: Its scores or metric validation do not validate our small corpus or numerical scorer.
sources.study_implication_inference: Keep retrieval/exposure/output metrics distinct and validate the selected automatic scoring rule on actual outputs.

sources.title: Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: ACM SACMAT 2026; official accepted regular-paper list verified
sources.publication_status_verified: Official conference acceptance and author publication page; full methods read from arXiv v2
full_text_read_locators: Sections 5.1.3–5.1.4: evaluation and equal one-text budgets
sources.establishes: Compares attacks at one poisoned text per target; v2 uses GPT-4o-mini judgment for ASR.
sources.does_not_establish: An LLM judge is not independent human validation; corpus/template conditions differ from ours.
sources.study_implication_inference: Match dose and targets when comparing attacks and distinguish text repetition from stronger individual poisons.
sources.bibliography_note: Current manuscript accurately cites v1, whose author order differs (Minghong Fang third). Updating to v2 requires updating year/order and methods attribution together. ACM DOI endpoint returned 403, so publisher DOI/pages not verified from primary publisher.

sources.title: Towards More Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Evaluating RAG Under Adversarial Poisoning Attacks
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; no formal venue independently verified
sources.establishes: Separates adversarial, untouched, and guiding contexts; prompting effects vary across models.
sources.does_not_establish: Its context interventions are not identical to our KB-insertion unrelated control.
sources.study_implication_inference: Use equal-exposure context analysis to isolate generator behavior from retrieval effects.

sources.title: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
sources.venue: IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML) 2026
sources.publication_status_verified: Official SaTML 2026 program and arXiv v2 full text
full_text_read_locators: Sections II-B–II-D: corruption model and robustness definition
sources.establishes: Certifies quality bounds for a defined number of corrupted retrieved passages under an explicit model.
sources.does_not_establish: Its guarantees do not transfer to supplied-label filtering or arbitrary whole-KB poisoning.
sources.study_implication_inference: Specify attacker control and distinguish empirical absence of successes from certified robustness.

sources.title: Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: arXiv preprint; also labeled preprint on author publication page
sources.establishes: Distinguishes targeted/DoS/triggered DoS and evaluates effects of expanded correct-answer evidence.
sources.does_not_establish: Benchmark-wide statements do not certify our metadata gate or make UNKNOWN universally a defense success.
sources.study_implication_inference: Record clean evidence density and separate targeted wrong answers, abstentions, and other failures.

sources.title: RAGPart & RAGMask: Retrieval-Stage Defenses Against Corpus Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
sources.venue: arXiv metadata reports AAAI 2026 Workshop on New Frontiers in Information Retrieval, oral
sources.publication_status_verified: Preprint text and author-supplied workshop comment verified; independent workshop proceedings not inspected
full_text_read_locators: Section 4: ASR means at least one poison retrieved; SR means at least one golden document retrieved
sources.establishes: Tests retrieval defenses; its ASR is poison inclusion, not generation of a targeted false answer.
sources.does_not_establish: TF-IDF reranking implements neither method; a workshop is not main AAAI; older criticism of RobustRAG should not be transferred to its revised v2 without analysis.
sources.study_implication_inference: Pair attack reduction with supporting-evidence and clean-utility measures; use as positioning, not an unrun baseline.

sources.title: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.version_note: Official Rev.5 publication with December 2020 updates; page also describes Release 5.2.0 of August 2025
full_text_read_locators: AU-9 audit protection including cryptographic protection
SI-7 information integrity including cryptographic protection
sources.establishes: Defines organizational access, change, audit, and integrity controls.
sources.does_not_establish: It provides no RAG ASR result or guarantee that authenticated content is factually correct.
sources.study_implication_inference: Model who issues trust labels, who may alter them, how changes are evidenced, and what compromise means.

bibliography_findings.finding: v1 citation matches its 2025 author order. v2/SACMAT2026 changes order and evaluation details; update attribution consistently if adopting v2.
v2 year 2026 is correct; official SaTML2026 program confirms conference identity. Publisher DOI/pages not verified here.
Preprint submitted December2025; arXiv comment reports an AAAI2026 workshop, not main AAAI.
Trailing RAG SECURITY RESEARCH is a copied PDF header, not citation content.
Current URL contains a literal space after eacl-. The canonical link must be verified and corrected; RAGAs content not evaluated in this subtask.

methodological_inferences: A fixed target set at one positive dose is not a fixed-target multi-dose experiment.
Whole-pipeline targeted-versus-unrelated insertion contrasts do not isolate generator susceptibility under equal exposure.
Exact repetition, diverse poison, and broader target coverage require separate intervention labels.
Zero scored successes under labels that perfectly identify all insertions measures an idealized eligibility boundary, not detector accuracy.
A label-change control is distinct from unauthorized change of a protected provenance system.
Cross-paper ASRs cannot rank methods without aligning threat model, budget, evidence density, generator, and scoring.
limitations: No new LLM calls, new attack runs, or original-manuscript edits were made.
No independent human response judgments were produced.
Publisher DOI endpoint for SACMAT paper returned access failure; no unverified DOI was promoted as verified.
Recommendations are implications for the upcoming plan, not claims that every source implements every listed control.
